This message comes from Schwab.
Investing with Schwab is like a hike with endless trails.
Go solo with self-directed investing,
take stops along the way with trading,
or choose a guide with full service wealth management.
Whatever trails you take,
you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington,
I'm Corva Coleman.
Big tech company Invidia is investigating its own CEO, Jensen Huang.
The company is looking into whether Huang left himself open to spying by China.
Invidia makes some of the world's most sophisticated computer chips.
That has triggered debate about whether these computer chips should be sold to China.
NPR's John Rubich has more.
The board was following up on reports, not yet confirmed by NPR,
that CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a Chinese woman who US intelligence agencies
believe was recruited by China's main spy agency to gather information on him
and potentially to try to influence US policy.
Invidia did not mention China in its announcement online of the investigation,
but it did say the spark for this was reporting that Huang was,
"the target of a foreign intelligence effort."
NPR's John Rubich reporting.
Invidia also posted a memo that Huang sent to company staff.
He admitted to a romantic relationship and said he will cooperate with the board's investigation.
Meanwhile, the Chinese government says the spying allegations are unsubstantiated.
President Trump told 60 Minutes on CBS his mass deportation policies may have gone too far.
Trump's immigration policy leader, Stephen Miller,
starts work today as White House chief of staff.
Congressional Democrats say they intend to launch corruption investigations of President Trump's cabinet.
NPR's Rebecca Hersher reports.
In an interview on CNN's State of the Union program,
Attorney General Todd Blanche said congressional Democrats should not investigate members of the president's cabinet.
That is not oversight. I welcome oversight.
The president has asked for the Department of Justice to investigate Democratic lawmakers,
calling them extortionists.
Democratic Representative Robert Garcia, who heads the House Oversight Committee,
responded in an interview with the same CNN program.
They can come after us however they want. We're not going to be intimidated.
The sparring comes less than a week after the GOP's defeat in the midterm elections.
Rebecca Hersher, NPR News.
International climate change negotiations have kicked off today in Turkey.
The talks at the COP 31 summit began with a dire warning from international forecasters.
NPR's Lauren Summer has more.
The way 2026 is going, it's looking like it'll be one of the hottest years on record.
That means the last 12 years are the hottest 12 years since record keeping began,
according to a new report from the World Meteorological Organization.
Emissions from burning fossil fuels also led to a new record.
Heat-trapping gases in the atmosphere are now more than 50 percent higher than they were in 1750.
China emits the most greenhouse gases yearly, followed by the United States and India.
World leaders are negotiating their plans for reducing emissions from fossil fuels.
Most nations are not on track to meet their pledges.
Lauren Summer, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eizenkot has been tapped to try to form the country's next government.
His party did not win the most votes in recent elections compared to Israeli Prime Minister
Benjamin Netanyahu's, but other political parties still want Eizenkot to try.
Most schools across the U.S. ban cell phones in their classrooms.
And Biers Amy Held reports a growing number of teachers want to see
laptops removed from class to cut down on distractions and cheating.
Nine out of ten U.S. public schools provide a device to every student.
Maureen Mulvaney in Minneapolis has been teaching for 23 years and says she's noticed something.
Her students have lost stamina.
They look at something that's hard and they immediately turn to A.I. to solve the problem.
So last year she removed all screens from her high school A.P. literature class.
Real paperback.
Students read the classics and write essays by hand.
Their skills improve, she says.
What was really surprising was that the students liked it so much.
They were saying, why can't we do this in all our classes?
More are moving in that direction.
A recent Gallup poll finds nearly two-thirds of teachers say students should spend less time
on screens, but roughly the same say some digital tools can be helpful.
Amy Held, NPR News.
NASA says it's taking applications again for people who want to be astronauts.
Applicants need to be U.S. citizens and have at least a master's degree in a STEM field.
The process is difficult.
The last time NASA saw an astronaut's more than 8,000 people applied, 10 people were selected.
This is NPR.
